lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: personal operations map

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic personal operations map task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Before the capstone week starts, the learner builds a one-page personal operations map: one row per system, a specific real task they actually did for that system in the past month, and a confidence rating, so they can see clearly which systems are strong and which need attention during the week ahead.
safetyNotes: This is a private planning and self-assessment page; it is not shared outside the household as part of this lesson.
materials: learner-local: paper or a document for the one-page operations map
learner-local: the learner's task sheets or notes from Units 1 through 5

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain how two of your five systems connect to each other in your real life (for example, how a food task depends on a planning task), and what that connection means for how you'll approach the capstone week.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity. | Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner identify one place where two systems overlap in practice (for example, a food task that also requires a transportation trip) and describe the overlap in one specific sentence.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic personal operations map task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: personal operations map worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before the capstone week starts, the learner builds a one-page personal operations map: one row per system, a specific real task they actually did for that system in the past month, and a confidence rating, so they can see clearly which systems are strong and which need attention during the week ahead.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact personal operations map decision or action.
Model move 2: List the five systems you have studied this year and write a one-line description of what each one actually manages.
Model move 3: For each of the five systems, name one specific real task you actually did in the past month, not a general category.

Model check: System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity. | Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system.

resources.title: personal operations map action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for personal operations map.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: personal operations map coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before the capstone week starts, the learner builds a one-page personal operations map: one row per system, a specific real task they actually did for that system in the past month, and a confidence rating, so they can see clearly which systems are strong and which need attention during the week ahead.
Coach direction: List the five systems you have studied this year and write a one-line description of what each one actually manages.
Learner prompt: List the five systems (planning, household, food, transportation, communication) with a one-line description of what each one manages in your real life.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: personal operations map complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the five systems, name one specific real task you actually did in the past month, not a general category.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named one specific real task for the planning system (for example, building a weekly schedule or breaking a project into steps).
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named one specific real task for the household system (for example, a cleaning, laundry, or supply-checking task).
Response 3 (t2-p3): I named one specific real task for the food system (for example, planning a week of meals or checking a listed price).
Response 4 (t2-p4): I named one specific real task for the transportation system (for example, planning a route or checking a schedule).
Response 5 (t2-p5): I named one specific real task for the communication system (for example, drafting a message with a clear request).
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: personal operations map minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain how two of your five systems connect to each other in your real life (for example, how a food task depends on a planning task), and what that connection means for how you'll approach the capstone week.

Success checks: System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity. | Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: personal operations map supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional personal operations map condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity. | Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: Before the capstone week starts, the learner builds a one-page personal operations map: one row per system, a specific real task they actually did for that system in the past month, and a confidence rating, so they can see clearly which systems are strong and which need attention during the week ahead.

simulationRoute.title: personal operations map — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the personal operations map task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain how two of your five systems connect to each other in your real life (for example, how a food task depends on a planning task), and what that connection means for how you'll approach the capstone week.
observableCriteria: System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity.
Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: System coverage and specificity: Names all five systems with one specific real task example for each, drawn from actual recent activity. | Confidence self-assessment accuracy: Confidence ratings are given for all five systems, with a reasoning-based explanation for the identified weakest system.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
